title: The Shared Marquee (Part 2)
description: Two boxes went out the back on Saturday. One holds the Hendersons' wedding cake, one holds Linda's late uncle, and nobody wrote on either of them. Donna and Phil call back in to sort out which box is which before two families arrive at the same shared front door, while the marquee is now down to a single S.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: You're back on Snazzie FM. When we left off, Donna runs the funerals, Phil runs the weddings, same building, and on Saturday two big white boxes went out the back. One is a wedding cake. One is Linda's uncle. Donna, Phil... please tell me you know which is which.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: I'd like that on the record too. Which box is the man, Ronnie.

lines.speaker: caller-donna
lines.text: I'm standing in the cooler right now, Ronnie. There are two boxes. With respect, they are identical. Phil ordered matching boxes.

lines.speaker: caller-phil
lines.text: Love is love, Donna, and matching is elegant. A bride doesn't want a box that clashes.

lines.speaker: caller-donna
lines.text: Neither does my uncle, Phil! Sorry, HER uncle. Linda's uncle. The point is one of these boxes has a person in it and they look exactly the same!

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Can you just... open one?

lines.speaker: caller-donna
lines.text: I am not opening a box on the radio, Barry.

lines.speaker: caller-phil
lines.text: One of them is heavier. The cake had three tiers. Pick up a box, Donna.

lines.speaker: caller-donna
lines.text: ...They weigh the same, Phil. <p:0.3> Why do they weigh the same.

lines.speaker: caller-phil
lines.text: Big cake. <p:0.3> Very big cake.

lines.speaker: caller-linda
lines.text: Hi, it's Linda again. Sorry. <p:0.3> My family's already in the parking lot. Should I tell them to come in, or...

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Not yet, Linda. We're verifying the boxes.

lines.speaker: caller-linda
lines.text: Oh. The other family's here too. The Hendersons. They're already arguing with my cousins about a parking spot.

lines.speaker: caller-donna
lines.text: Because there's ONE spot, Phil! ONE! You painted a heart on the other one!

lines.speaker: caller-phil
lines.text: Love is love, Donna, and love needs to park.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Okay, the boxes. Is there a label? A tag? Anything written on them?

lines.speaker: caller-donna
lines.text: There's a card on each. <p:0.3> They both say CONGRATULATIONS, Phil. WHY does my uncle's box say congratulations.

lines.speaker: caller-phil
lines.text: We share a card printer. It only had the one template loaded.

lines.speaker: caller-donna
lines.text: We do NOT share a printer!

lines.speaker: caller-phil
lines.text: It's a SHARED printer, Donna! Same as the trolley! Same as the letters!

lines.speaker: caller-donna
lines.text: Do not bring up the letters! My sign out front says one S! ONE S, Phil, for two families walking up RIGHT NOW!

lines.speaker: caller-linda
lines.text: Oh, that's why everyone's confused at the door. The sign just says S.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Wait. Both families are at the one door. Reading one S.

lines.speaker: caller-phil
lines.text: I'll fix it. I'll move the S to the top so it's clearly a wedding.

lines.speaker: caller-donna
lines.text: You touch that S and I will put YOU on the casket cart, Phil!

lines.speaker: caller-linda
lines.text: [sigh] Um. <p:0.3> My uncle's box just got wheeled out front. By a Henderson. They think it's the cake.

lines.speaker: caller-donna
lines.text: STOP THAT MAN. <p:0.3> Phil, that is a PERSON, not a dessert!

lines.speaker: caller-phil
lines.text: Then where's the cake?!

lines.speaker: caller-linda
lines.text: Oh, the cake's fine. They're cutting it now. <p:0.3> At the funeral.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: They're cutting the cake. At the funeral.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Well, folks, the boxes are sorted, sort of. The Hendersons have a man, the mourners have a cake, and out front, one beautiful sign that simply says S. <p:0.3> We'll be right back, soon as somebody figures out who's giving the toast.

lines.speaker: caller-linda
lines.text: ...They asked me. <p:0.3> Should I do the wedding speech or the eulogy?
